Check diversity estimates against heuristic plausibility ranges

Source: R/validation.R
checkDiversityPlausibility.Rd

Compares observed diversity metrics against wide plausibility ranges for common pathogens, as a check on units and orders of magnitude. The ranges are heuristic: they are the package's own, set generously enough that a correctly computed estimate on a typical data set falls inside them, and they are not taken from the literature or from any study. Each is listed in Details. A value inside its range is therefore no evidence that an estimate is correct, and one outside it most often points to a unit, depth or QC problem rather than to biology.

Usage

checkDiversityPlausibility(
  div_df,
  pathogen = c("sars_cov_2", "influenza", "hiv", "tb", "generic")
)

Arguments

div_df

A DataFrame or data.frame with columns metric and value, or containing diversity columns such as pi and shannon (as returned by calcDiversity), with an optional sample_id.

pathogen

Character scalar. Pathogen whose plausibility range is used. One of "sars_cov_2", "influenza", "hiv", "tb", or "generic".

Value

A DataFrame with one row per sample and metric and columns:

sample_id

Sample identifier, taken from div_df when it has that column, otherwise the row number; NA for long input.

metric

Diversity metric name.

observed

Observed value.

expected_min

Lower bound of the plausibility range.

expected_max

Upper bound of the plausibility range.

in_range

Logical; whether the observed value falls within the range, and FALSE when the value is missing.

Details

The ranges, per site for \(\pi\) and on the scale calcDiversity returns for Shannon entropy:

pathogenpishannon
sars_cov_21e-6 to 1e-30 to 15
influenza1e-5 to 5e-30 to 20
hiv1e-4 to 5e-20 to 30
tb1e-9 to 1e-40 to 5
generic0 to 10 to 100

A wide table, as calcDiversity returns, is checked row by row, one row per sample and metric; a long table with metric and value columns is checked as given. Metrics without a range are left out.

Examples

div <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = c("a", "b"),
    pi = c(1e-4, 0.3), shannon = c(5.0, 7.5))
checkDiversityPlausibility(div, pathogen = "sars_cov_2")
#> DataFrame with 4 rows and 6 columns
#>     sample_id      metric  observed expected_min expected_max  in_range
#>   <character> <character> <numeric>    <numeric>    <numeric> <logical>
#> 1           a          pi    0.0001        1e-06        0.001      TRUE
#> 2           b          pi    0.3000        1e-06        0.001     FALSE
#> 3           a     shannon    5.0000        0e+00       15.000      TRUE
#> 4           b     shannon    7.5000        0e+00       15.000      TRUE
